matt: Quick contract check before I update SDK docs — embeddings endpoint behavior for v2: what are the supported input shapes (string vs array vs object), how do we handle truncation, what's the per-request batch limit, and can we assert vector shape reliably? cc @jen @alex
jen: We accept `input` as either a single string or an array. Array items can be plain strings or small objects `{id, text}` — if object, we use `text`. This is backward-compatible with v1.
alex: Truncation is per-item and tokenized using the model's tokenizer. We truncate to the model max input length (left-side keep, drop tail). We also set a per-item flag in the response metadata when truncation occurred: e.g. `truncated:true`.
sara: Batch limits: API enforces a max of 512 items per request for the hosted endpoint. If you hit it you get 413 with a message: "batch too large, max 512 items". There's also a payload size cap (~10MB) that can bite if you send huge docs as a single string.
matt: Good to know. What about empty inputs or nulls inside arrays? And do we ever return `null` vectors?
jen: We never return `null` for a valid text input. Empty string -> returns embedding (deterministic). `null`/missing items in the array are rejected with 400. If you want to skip an item, drop it client-side.
alex: Vector shape: dimension is model-specific and guaranteed consistent for a given model version. We include `model` and `vector_dim` in the response envelope so SDKs can assert shape. Example response (abridged):
```
{
  "model": "rwd-embed-v1",
  "vector_dim": 1536,
  "data": [ [0.001, -0.32, ...], [ ... ] ],
  "truncated": [false, true]
}
```
jen: Also note we return embeddings in float32 by default. Future low-precision options (fp16/int8) will be opt-in and documented in the model catalog — not the default.
sara: For large-batch processing we recommend streaming or chunking: if you need >512 items, split client-side into multiple requests or use our batch job API (dedicated customers) which supports bigger jobs.
ci-bot: integration-tests/embeddings: added contract test that asserts `vector_dim` present, `data.length == input.length`, and `truncated` is same length as inputs — all green on staging.
matt: Perfect — I'll update SDK to check `vector_dim` and fail fast on mismatched lengths, add guidance about chunking, and include note about `truncated` bits. I'll open a PR and tag @jen for docs review. :+1:
jen: Thanks! One more tiny note — keeping left-most tokens preserves prefixes for search use-cases. Document that in the truncation section.
matt: Got it, will include that.
